text:
alex (Eng Manager): Need guidance. We promoted an IC from L3->L4 last month but want the effective date to be the start of the project (2026-03-01). Can promotions be backdated and do we do retro pay? Also worried about how this affects their bonus target and quota.

nina (People Ops): Short: backdating is allowed but limited. We can set an earlier effective date up to 60 days retro from the submission date. Anything older requires exec sign-off and payroll justification. Retro pay (backpay) is optional but can be requested; finance will review.

alex (Eng Manager): Ok 60 days should cover it. What's the exact workflow to request backpay?

dave (People Ops): Submit a Comp Change Request and check the "Request Backpay" box. Attach the promotion note, signed manager approval, and a timeline of the work that justifies the earlier date. We need the payroll code and effective date in the form.

payroll-bot: Reminder: payroll system requires all backpay approvals before 2026-05-05 17:00 PDT to process in May payroll. See https://intra.redwood/payroll/backpay-policy

olga (Compensation): A couple notes: backpay is paid as a lump sum and is taxed in the period it's issued. Equity/proration is handled separately. If the promotion changes bonus target or commission, we recalc target from effective date; sales should notify sales ops for quota changes.

mike (Finance): From finance: include GL code and cost center. We'll need to forecast the incremental headcount spend for the current quarter. Backpay > $5k or comp moves >15% require compensation committee review.

alex (Eng Manager): Got it. What about retroactive equity? We want to grant a small refresh with grant date aligned to the promotion date. Any constraints?

sara (HRBP): Equity grant date can be backdated only to the promotion effective date if within 30 days, otherwise grant will use the submission date. Also need manager + HRBP sign-off.

lina (IC): Quick question as the impacted person: will this change my next performance calibration or my manager's feedback window?

nina (People Ops): Good Q. Promotion changes will be reflected in the next calibration cycle. If you were promoted mid-cycle we'll include you in the next calibration as L4, and your manager should update your scorecard now. No change to prior feedback windows.

alex (Eng Manager): Any suggested wording for the timeline doc? I want a crisp one-pager for the committee if needed.

dave (People Ops): Keep it concise: 1-line summary, timeline bullets (dates & deliverables), 3 evidence points (impact/metrics), list of peers/benchmarks, requested comp + backpay amount, and requested effective date. Example snippet: 

```
Summary: Promote to L4 effective 2026-03-01 based on ownership of X project.
Timeline:
 - 2026-02-10: took tech lead on X
 - 2026-02-28: shipped feature Y impacting N customers
Evidence: increased deployment freq, owned oncall for X, mentored 2 ICs
Requested comp: +12% base, backpay = $2,400 (mar-apr)
```

alex (Eng Manager): Nice example, thanks. If the comp committee is needed, how long do approvals usually take? We might miss payroll cutoff.

olga (Compensation): Committee meets every Thursday at 10am. Normal queue is 1-2 business days; for larger requests add the "expedite" flag with justification. If you miss payroll cutoff we'll set a formal effective date and pay the adjustment next payroll.

mike (Finance): Also note: for mid-quarter cost forecasts we need the approval memo to update headcount spend. If you want the finance ops team to pre-approve estimate, tag @mike.

alex (Eng Manager): Will do. Thanks everyone. I'll attach the one-pager + updated scorecard in the Comp Change form and mark "Request Backpay". Tagging @sara to co-sign.

sara (HRBP): I'll review the draft before submission. Drop it here or DM. Happy to co-sign once the evidence is ready.

alex (Eng Manager): Dropping the draft here in 15m. Appreciate the quick help. :pray:
